column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|01-01|1484|Ούλριχ Ζβίγγλιος|Ulrich Zwingli|Ulrich Zwingli was a priest in Zurich and became a leading figure of the Reformation in Switzerland. He preached against practices of the Catholic Church and promoted a simpler form of worship. He was killed in 1531 at the Battle of Kappel, in the war between the cantons.

bio|01-01|1735|Πολ Ρίβιρ|Paul Revere|Paul Revere was a silversmith in Boston and a patriot in the American Revolution. He became known for his midnight ride of 1775, with which he warned of the British advance towards Lexington and Concord. His name became a symbol of the revolution.

bio|01-01|1863|Πιερ ντε Κουμπερτέν|Pierre de Coubertin|The French baron Pierre de Coubertin was an educator and historian who was inspired to revive the Olympic Games. In 1894 he founded the International Olympic Committee, and in 1896 the first modern Games were held in Athens. He was president of the Committee until 1925.

bio|01-01|1894|Χάινριχ Χερτζ|Heinrich Hertz|Heinrich Hertz was a German physicist who proved experimentally the existence of electromagnetic waves, which Maxwell had predicted. He died young, at thirty-six. The unit of frequency, the hertz, bears his name.

bio|01-01|1919|Τζερόμ Ντέιβιντ Σάλιντζερ|Jerome David Salinger|J. D. Salinger was an American writer. He became famous with the novel "The Catcher in the Rye" in 1951, which tells of the teenage alienation of Holden Caulfield. Later he withdrew from public life and published very little.

bio|01-01|1944|Ομάρ ελ-Μπεσίρ|Omar al-Bashir|Omar al-Bashir was an officer in the Sudanese army and took power in a coup in 1989. He ruled the country for thirty years. The International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant against him for crimes in Darfur, and he was overthrown in 2019.

bio|01-01|1992|Γκρέις Μάρεϊ Χόπερ|Grace Murray Hopper|Grace Hopper was an American mathematician and naval officer and a pioneer of computing. She created one of the first compilers and contributed to the COBOL language. She died in 1992 at the age of eighty-five.

bio|01-01|1995|Γιουτζίν Γουίγκνερ|Eugene Wigner|Eugene Wigner was born in Hungary and lived in the United States. He was a physicist and contributed to quantum physics and to the theory of symmetries. In 1963 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|01-02|1642|Μωάμεθ Δ΄|Mehmed IV|Mehmed IV was an Ottoman sultan from 1648 to 1687. He became sultan as a child and power was exercised by the Köprülü grand viziers. He lost the Battle of Vienna in 1683 and was deposed.

bio|01-02|1822|Ρούντολφ Κλαούζιους|Rudolf Clausius|Rudolf Clausius was a German physicist. He founded thermodynamics, formulated its second law and introduced the concept of entropy. He taught at universities in Germany and Switzerland.

bio|01-02|1837|Μίλι Μπαλάκιρεφ|Mily Balakirev|Mily Balakirev was a Russian composer and pianist and the leader of "The Five", a group of composers who wanted a Russian national music. He wrote the piano piece "Islamey", known for its difficulty.

bio|01-02|1861|Φρειδερίκος Γουλιέλμος Δ΄|Frederick William IV|Frederick William IV was king of Prussia from 1840. He rejected constitutional monarchy and in 1849 refused the crown of a united Germany offered by the Frankfurt Assembly. In his last years he was ill and was replaced by his brother William.

bio|01-02|1873|Τερέζ ντε Λισιέ|Thérèse of Lisieux|Thérèse of Lisieux was born in France and became a Carmelite nun. She wrote the autobiography "Story of a Soul" and died young, at twenty-four. The Catholic Church declared her a saint and a Doctor of the Church.

bio|01-02|1892|Τζωρτζ Αίρυ|George Airy|George Airy was a British astronomer and mathematician. He served as Astronomer Royal and directed the Greenwich Observatory, where he established the prime meridian used as the basis of world time.

bio|01-02|1917|Έντουαρντ Μπάρνετ Τάιλορ|Edward Burnett Tylor|Edward Tylor was an English anthropologist and is considered one of the founders of cultural anthropology. In his book "Primitive Culture" he defines culture and argues for the evolution of societies.

bio|01-02|1920|Ισαάκ Ασίμοφ|Isaac Asimov|Isaac Asimov was born in Russia and grew up in the United States. He was a biochemist and wrote an enormous number of books, science fiction novels and popular science works. The "Foundation" series and the three laws of robotics are well known.

bio|01-02|1950|Εμίλ Γιάνινγκς|Emil Jannings|Emil Jannings was a German actor born in Switzerland. He worked in silent and sound film and starred in Murnau's "The Last Laugh". In 1929 he became the first winner of the Oscar for Best Actor.

bio|01-03|1322|Φίλιππος Ε΄|Philip V|Philip V the Tall was king of France from 1316 to 1322. He came to the throne by excluding women from the succession and strengthened the administration of the state. He died without a son and was succeeded by his brother.

bio|01-03|1883|Κλέμεντ Άττλη|Clement Attlee|Clement Attlee was a British Labour politician. He became prime minister in 1945 after his party's victory, and his government founded the National Health Service. Under his government India became independent.

bio|01-03|1892|Τζ. Ρ. Ρ. Τόλκιν|J. R. R. Tolkien|J. R. R. Tolkien was born in South Africa and lived in England, where he taught language and philology at Oxford. He wrote "The Hobbit" and "The Lord of the Rings". He created an entire fantasy mythology and influenced the fantasy genre.

bio|01-03|1907|Ρέι Μιλάντ|Ray Milland|Ray Milland was born in Wales and became a film actor in Britain and the United States. In 1946 he won the Oscar for Best Actor for "The Lost Weekend", in which he played an alcoholic writer.

bio|01-03|1923|Γιάροσλαβ Χάσεκ|Jaroslav Hašek|Jaroslav Hašek was a Czech writer. He wrote the satirical novel "The Good Soldier Švejk" during the First World War. The work remained unfinished and he died in 1923, aged forty-one.

bio|01-03|1931|Ζοζέφ Ζοφρ|Joseph Joffre|Joseph Joffre was a French general. He was commander-in-chief of the French forces at the start of the First World War and contributed to the victory at the Battle of the Marne in 1914. He was later replaced and was honoured with the title of marshal.

bio|01-03|1956|Μελ Γκίμπσον|Mel Gibson|Mel Gibson was born in the United States and grew up in Australia. He became known as an actor in the films "Mad Max" and "Lethal Weapon" and as director of "Braveheart", which won an Oscar. He also directed "The Passion of the Christ".

bio|01-03|1969|Μίχαελ Σουμάχερ|Michael Schumacher|Michael Schumacher was born in Germany and won seven Formula 1 world championships, two with Benetton and five with Ferrari. He was one of the greatest drivers in history. In 2013 he suffered a serious skiing accident.

bio|01-03|2003|Γκρέτα Τούνμπεργκ|Greta Thunberg|Greta Thunberg was born in Sweden. In 2018, at the age of fifteen, she started a protest strike for the climate on her own outside the Swedish parliament. She became a symbol of the international youth climate movement.

bio|01-04|1643|Ισαάκ Νεύτων|Isaac Newton|Isaac Newton was an English physicist and mathematician. He formulated the laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation in the "Principia" and laid the foundations of calculus. He also carried out pioneering research in optics.

bio|01-04|1785|Γιάκομπ Γκριμ|Jacob Grimm|Jacob Grimm was a German philologist and folklorist. Together with his brother Wilhelm he collected and published the fairy tales of the Brothers Grimm. He also made important studies of the Germanic languages and formulated "Grimm's law".

bio|01-04|1809|Λουί Μπράιγ|Louis Braille|Louis Braille became blind as a child in France. At fifteen he devised the system of writing with raised dots that is read with the fingers. The Braille system is used by blind people throughout the world.

bio|01-04|1940|Μπράιαν Τζόζεφσον|Brian Josephson|Brian Josephson is a Welsh physicist. He studied the superconducting tunnelling effect, which he predicted and which is called the Josephson effect. In 1973 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|01-04|1941|Ανρί Μπεργκσόν|Henri Bergson|Henri Bergson was a French philosopher and taught at the Collège de France. He developed the concepts of duration and creative evolution. In 1927 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|01-04|1960|Αλμπέρ Καμύ|Albert Camus|Albert Camus was born in Algeria and became a writer and philosopher. He wrote "The Stranger" and "The Myth of Sisyphus" and founded the philosophy of the absurd. In 1957 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He was killed in a car accident in 1960.

bio|01-04|1961|Έρβιν Σρέντινγκερ|Erwin Schrödinger|Erwin Schrödinger was an Austrian physicist and one of the founders of quantum mechanics. He formulated the equation that bears his name and the thought experiment of "Schrödinger's cat". In 1933 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|01-04|1965|Τόμας Στερνς Έλιοτ|T. S. Eliot|T. S. Eliot was born in the United States and lived in England, where he became a British citizen. He was a poet and critic and wrote "The Waste Land", a poem that marked modernism. In 1948 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|01-04|1990|Τόνι Κρόος|Toni Kroos|Toni Kroos was born in Germany and is a midfielder. He played for Bayern Munich and Real Madrid and won the 2014 World Cup with Germany. He was known for his precise passing.

bio|01-05|1589|Αικατερίνη των Μεδίκων|Catherine de' Medici|Catherine de' Medici was born in Florence and became queen of France as the wife of Henry II. After his death she exerted influence as the mother of kings. She is associated with the French Wars of Religion and with the St Bartholomew's Day massacre.

bio|01-05|1876|Κόνραντ Αντενάουερ|Konrad Adenauer|Konrad Adenauer was a German politician, mayor of Cologne before the Second World War. He became the first chancellor of West Germany, from 1949 to 1963. He supported reconciliation with France and membership of NATO.

bio|01-05|1932|Ουμπέρτο Έκο|Umberto Eco|Umberto Eco was an Italian semiotician and professor. He became famous with his novel "The Name of the Rose", published in 1980, and also wrote essays and other novels such as "Foucault's Pendulum".

bio|01-05|1933|Κάλβιν Κούλιτζ|Calvin Coolidge|Calvin Coolidge was the 30th president of the United States, from 1923 to 1929. He became president after the death of Harding and followed a policy of small government and limited spending, in a period of economic growth.

bio|01-05|1938|Χουάν Κάρλος Α΄|Juan Carlos I|Juan Carlos I became king of Spain in 1975, after the death of Franco. He helped the country's transition to democracy and opposed the failed coup of 1981. He abdicated in 2014 in favour of his son Felipe.

bio|01-05|1956|Φρανκ-Βάλτερ Στάινμαϊερ|Frank-Walter Steinmeier|Frank-Walter Steinmeier is a German politician of the Social Democratic Party. He served as foreign minister and vice-chancellor in the governments of Angela Merkel and since 2017 he has been federal president of Germany, an office that is mainly ceremonial.

bio|01-05|1970|Μαξ Μπορν|Max Born|Max Born was born in Breslau and was a physicist who contributed to quantum mechanics, particularly with the probabilistic interpretation of the wave function. In 1954 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|01-05|1975|Μπράντλεϊ Κούπερ|Bradley Cooper|Bradley Cooper is an American actor and producer. He became known with "The Hangover" and starred in films such as "Silver Linings Playbook" and "American Sniper". He has been nominated for an Oscar many times.

bio|01-05|2014|Εουσέμπιο|Eusébio|Eusébio was a footballer from Mozambique who played for Portugal and Benfica. He was a pioneer of his time and top scorer at the 1966 World Cup, where Portugal finished third. He died in 2014.

bio|01-06|1412|Ζαν ντ' Αρκ|Joan of Arc|Joan of Arc, the "Maid of Lorraine", was a French peasant girl who believed she was guided by divine voices. She helped Charles VII in the Hundred Years' War and led the French in lifting the siege of Orléans. She was condemned and burned in 1431 and later became a saint.

bio|01-06|1878|Καρλ Σάντμπεργκ|Carl Sandburg|Carl Sandburg was an American poet and biographer. He wrote poetry about Chicago and the lives of workers and a biography of Abraham Lincoln, for which he was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for History.

bio|01-06|1883|Χαλίλ Γκιμπράν|Kahlil Gibran|Kahlil Gibran was born in Lebanon and lived most of his years in the United States. He was a poet and painter and wrote the book "The Prophet" in English, which has been translated into dozens of languages.

bio|01-06|1884|Γκρέγκορ Μέντελ|Gregor Mendel|Gregor Mendel was an Augustinian monk and botanist in Moravia. With experiments on pea plants he discovered the basic rules of heredity. His work was recognised after his death and made him the father of genetics.

bio|01-06|1918|Γκέοργκ Κάντορ|Georg Cantor|Georg Cantor was born in Russia and lived in Germany. He was a mathematician and founded set theory and the study of infinite sets. His ideas were disputed in his time but later became a foundation of mathematics.

bio|01-06|1919|Θεόδωρος Ρούζβελτ|Theodore Roosevelt|Theodore Roosevelt was the 26th president of the United States, from 1901 to 1909. He became president after the assassination of McKinley. He made reforms against monopolies and for the protection of nature, and in 1906 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|01-06|1924|Κιμ Ντε-τζουνγκ|Kim Dae-jung|Kim Dae-jung was a South Korean politician and campaigner for democracy. He was imprisoned and sentenced to death under a dictatorship and became president in 1998. He followed the "Sunshine Policy" towards North Korea and in 2000 was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|01-06|1955|Ρόουαν Άτκινσον|Rowan Atkinson|Rowan Atkinson is an English actor and comedian. He became known worldwide with his character "Mr. Bean" and starred in the series "Blackadder". In his early years he had studied electrical engineering.

bio|01-06|2022|Σίντνεϊ Πουατιέ|Sidney Poitier|Sidney Poitier was born in Miami and grew up in the Bahamas. He became the first African American to win the Oscar for Best Actor, in 1964 for "Lilies of the Field". He also starred in "Guess Who's Coming to Dinner".

bio|01-07|1536|Αικατερίνη της Αραγονίας|Catherine of Aragon|Catherine of Aragon was queen of England as the first wife of Henry VIII. Because they had no male heir, the king sought an annulment of the marriage, and as a result England broke away from the Catholic Church. She died in 1536.

bio|01-07|1800|Μίλαρντ Φίλμορ|Millard Fillmore|Millard Fillmore was the 13th president of the United States. He was vice-president and became president in 1850 after the death of Zachary Taylor. He signed the Compromise of 1850 on slavery and remained in office until 1853.

bio|01-07|1873|Σαρλ Πεγκί|Charles Péguy|Charles Péguy was a French poet and essayist. He was a socialist and later a Catholic and published the journal "Cahiers de la Quinzaine". He was killed in 1914 at the Battle of the Marne, at the start of the First World War.

bio|01-07|1943|Νίκολα Τέσλα|Nikola Tesla|Nikola Tesla was born in Smiljan, in present-day Croatia, and lived in the United States. He was an inventor and electrical engineer and developed the alternating current system, the induction motor and the Tesla coil. He died poor in 1943.

bio|01-07|1964|Νίκολας Κέιτζ|Nicolas Cage|Nicolas Cage is an American actor, a nephew of the director Francis Ford Coppola. He won the Oscar for Best Actor for "Leaving Las Vegas" and starred in "The Rock".
bio|01-07|1971|Τζέρεμι Ρένερ|Jeremy Renner|Jeremy Renner is an American actor. He was nominated for an Oscar for "The Hurt Locker" and "The Town". He is known as Hawkeye in the Avengers films.

bio|01-07|1984|Αλφρέντ Καστλέρ|Alfred Kastler|Alfred Kastler was a French physicist. He developed a method of optical pumping that allows the study of the energy levels of atoms. In 1966 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|01-07|1985|Λιούις Χάμιλτον|Lewis Hamilton|Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula 1 driver. He won seven world championships, six with Mercedes and one with McLaren, and broke many records. He was the first Black driver to win the championship.

bio|01-07|1989|Χιροχίτο|Hirohito|Hirohito was emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989. The country fought in the Second World War and in 1945 he announced its surrender. After the war he lost his divine status and became the symbolic head of state.

bio|01-08|1324|Μάρκο Πόλο|Marco Polo|Marco Polo was born in Venice and travelled to Asia with his father and uncle. He lived for years at the court of Kublai Khan. His account of his travels, the "Book of the Marvels of the World", made Asia known to Europeans.

bio|01-08|1642|Γαλιλαίος Γαλιλέι|Galileo Galilei|Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer and physicist. He used the telescope to observe the moons of Jupiter and the phases of Venus and supported the heliocentric system. The Church condemned him in 1633 and he died under house arrest.

bio|01-08|1823|Άλφρεντ Ράσελ Γουάλας|Alfred Russel Wallace|Alfred Russel Wallace was a Welsh naturalist. He studied the nature of the Amazon and of Malaysia and, independently of Darwin, formulated the theory of natural selection. He is considered the father of biogeography.

bio|01-08|1896|Πωλ Βερλαίν|Paul Verlaine|Paul Verlaine was a French poet of symbolism and post-romanticism. He wrote poems with strong musicality, such as the collection "Fêtes galantes". His life was turbulent and he died poor in Paris.

bio|01-08|1935|Έλβις Πρίσλεϊ|Elvis Presley|Elvis Presley was born in Mississippi. He became the "king of rock and roll" in the 1950s and sold hundreds of millions of records. He also starred in many films and died in 1977.

bio|01-08|1942|Στίβεν Χόκινγκ|Stephen Hawking|Stephen Hawking was a British theoretical physicist. He studied black holes and the origin of the universe and wrote "A Brief History of Time". Despite the motor neurone disease that afflicted him from a young age, he worked as a professor at Cambridge.

bio|01-08|1947|Ντέιβιντ Μπάουι|David Bowie|David Bowie was an English singer and actor. He stood out for the changes in his appearance and his music, such as the album "The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust". He influenced many artists and died in 2016.

bio|01-08|1984|Κιμ Γιονγκ Ουν|Kim Jong-un|Kim Jong-un has been the supreme leader of North Korea since 2011, when his father Kim Jong-il died. He continues the nuclear weapons programme and has met leaders of other countries, among them the American president Trump.

bio|01-08|1996|Φρανσουά Μιτεράν|François Mitterrand|François Mitterrand was a French politician of the Socialist Party. He became president of France in 1981 and remained until 1995, two terms of seven years. He supported European integration and died a few months after leaving office.

bio|01-09|1799|Μαρία Γκαετάνα Ανιέζι|Maria Gaetana Agnesi|Maria Gaetana Agnesi was an Italian mathematician. She wrote one of the first systematic textbooks of calculus and taught in Bologna. A curve she studied bears the name "witch of Agnesi".

bio|01-09|1873|Ναπολέων Γ΄|Napoleon III|Napoleon III was a nephew of Napoleon I. He was elected president of France in 1848 and became emperor in 1852. He was defeated at the Battle of Sedan in 1870 by Prussia and went into exile in England, where he died in 1873.

bio|01-09|1878|Βίκτωρ Εμμανουήλ Β΄|Victor Emmanuel II|Victor Emmanuel II was king of Sardinia and in 1861 became the first king of united Italy. He was helped in the unification by Cavour and Garibaldi. He died in Rome in 1878.

bio|01-09|1890|Κάρελ Τσάπεκ|Karel Čapek|Karel Čapek was a Czech writer. He wrote the play "R.U.R.", in which the word "robot" is used for the first time, and the novel "War with the Newts". The word was in fact coined by his brother Josef.

bio|01-09|1908|Σιμόν ντε Μποβουάρ|Simone de Beauvoir|Simone de Beauvoir was a French philosopher and writer. She was the partner of Jean-Paul Sartre and wrote "The Second Sex", a foundational work of feminism, published in 1949.

bio|01-09|1913|Ρίτσαρντ Νίξον|Richard Nixon|Richard Nixon was the 37th president of the United States, from 1969 to 1974. He opened relations with China and ended American involvement in the Vietnam War. He resigned because of the Watergate scandal.

bio|01-09|1923|Κάθριν Μάνσφιλντ|Katherine Mansfield|Katherine Mansfield was born in New Zealand and lived in Europe. She was a short-story writer and is considered one of the great names of the genre. She died young of tuberculosis, aged thirty-four.

bio|01-09|1941|Τζόαν Μπαέζ|Joan Baez|Joan Baez is an American folk singer. She was associated with the civil rights movement and the struggle against the Vietnam War and sang at the March on Washington in 1963. She is also known as an activist.

bio|01-09|1982|Αικατερίνη|Catherine|Catherine, Duchess of Cambridge, was born in Reading, England, as Kate Middleton. She married Prince William in 2011. After the death of Queen Elizabeth II she became Princess of Wales.

bio|01-10|1778|Κάρολος Λινναίος|Carl Linnaeus|Carl Linnaeus was a Swedish botanist and physician. He created the system of two-name nomenclature for organisms, that is genus and species, which is still used today. He wrote the work "Systema Naturae".

bio|01-10|1880|Μανουέλ Αθάνια|Manuel Azaña|Manuel Azaña was a Spanish politician and writer. He became prime minister and then president of the Second Spanish Republic. He remained in office during the Spanish Civil War and died in exile in France.

bio|01-10|1903|Μπάρμπαρα Χέπγουορθ|Barbara Hepworth|Barbara Hepworth was a British sculptor. She created abstract sculptures from stone, wood and metal, with holes and curves. She was one of the most important artists of her time and lived in St Ives.

bio|01-10|1934|Λεονίντ Κραβτσούκ|Leonid Kravchuk|Leonid Kravchuk was a Ukrainian politician. After the dissolution of the Soviet Union he became the first president of independent Ukraine, from 1991 to 1994.

bio|01-10|1938|Ντόναλντ Κνουθ|Donald Knuth|Donald Knuth is an American computer scientist and professor. He wrote the multi-volume work "The Art of Computer Programming" and created the TeX typesetting system. In 1974 he was awarded the Turing Award.

bio|01-10|1945|Ροντ Στιούαρτ|Rod Stewart|Rod Stewart is a British singer and songwriter. He began in the 1960s and has sold hundreds of millions of records with songs such as "Maggie May" and "Sailing". He is known for his raspy voice.

bio|01-10|1957|Γκαμπριέλα Μιστράλ|Gabriela Mistral|Gabriela Mistral was a Chilean poet and teacher. In 1945 she became the first Latin American to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She also worked as a diplomat and died in New York in 1957.

bio|01-10|1971|Κοκό Σανέλ|Coco Chanel|Coco Chanel was born in France and was a fashion designer. She founded the house of Chanel, established the little black dress and the perfume Chanel No. 5 and freed women's clothing from corsets. She died in 1971.

bio|01-10|2016|Ντέιβιντ Μπάουι|David Bowie|David Bowie died in 2016, two days after the release of the album "Blackstar". He was an English singer who strongly influenced rock music and innovated in image and genre.

bio|01-11|347|Θεοδόσιος Α΄|Theodosius I|Theodosius I was Roman emperor from 379 to 395. He was a Spanish general and took over the eastern part of the empire. He made Christianity the official religion of the state and was the last to rule the empire united.

bio|01-11|1757|Αλεξάντερ Χάμιλτον|Alexander Hamilton|Alexander Hamilton was born in the Caribbean and became one of the Founding Fathers of the United States. He was the first Secretary of the Treasury and created the country's financial system. He was killed in a duel with Aaron Burr in 1804.

bio|01-11|1815|Τζον Α. Μακντόναλντ|John A. Macdonald|John A. Macdonald was born in Scotland and emigrated to Canada. He was one of the "Fathers of Confederation" and the first prime minister of Canada, from 1867. He played a key role in the union of the provinces.

bio|01-11|1842|Γουίλιαμ Τζέιμς|William James|William James was an American psychologist and philosopher and one of the founders of psychology in the United States. He wrote "The Principles of Psychology" and supported pragmatism. He also wrote about religious experience.

bio|01-11|1928|Τόμας Χάρντι|Thomas Hardy|Thomas Hardy was an English novelist and poet. His novels, such as "Tess of the d'Urbervilles" and "Jude the Obscure", are set in rural "Wessex" and examine the fate of man. In his last years he wrote mainly poetry.

bio|01-11|1941|Εμάνουελ Λάσκερ|Emanuel Lasker|Emanuel Lasker was a German chess player and mathematician. He was world chess champion for 27 years, from 1894 to 1921, longer than anyone else. Because of his Jewish origin he left Germany and died in New York.

bio|01-11|1975|Ματέο Ρέντσι|Matteo Renzi|Matteo Renzi is an Italian politician. He was mayor of Florence and in 2014 became prime minister of Italy as leader of the Democratic Party. He resigned in 2016 after a referendum on constitutional reform failed.

bio|01-11|2008|Έντμουντ Χίλαρι|Edmund Hillary|Edmund Hillary was a mountaineer from New Zealand. In 1953, together with the Sherpa Tenzing Norgay, he became the first person to reach the summit of Everest. Later he helped the Sherpas with schools and hospitals in Nepal.

bio|01-11|2014|Αριέλ Σαρόν|Ariel Sharon|Ariel Sharon was an Israeli general and politician. He served as a minister and from 2001 to 2006 as prime minister of Israel. In 2005 he ordered the withdrawal from the Gaza Strip. In 2006 he suffered a stroke and remained in a coma until his death.

bio|01-12|1519|Μαξιμιλιανός Α΄|Maximilian I|Maximilian I was Holy Roman Emperor from 1508. He belonged to the House of Habsburg and through marriages and alliances extended his family's influence in Europe. He was succeeded by his grandson Charles V.

bio|01-12|1665|Πιερ ντε Φερμά|Pierre de Fermat|Pierre de Fermat was a French lawyer and mathematician. He contributed to number theory and geometry and formulated "Fermat's Last Theorem", which was proved only in 1994 by Andrew Wiles.

bio|01-12|1729|Έντμουντ Μπερκ|Edmund Burke|Edmund Burke was born in Dublin and became a British politician and philosopher. He supported the American colonists but criticised the French Revolution in "Reflections on the Revolution in France". He is considered the father of modern conservatism.

bio|01-12|1876|Τζακ Λόντον|Jack London|Jack London was an American writer. He himself went to the Klondike for gold and this experience inspired him. He wrote the novels "The Call of the Wild" and "White Fang".

bio|01-12|1893|Χέρμαν Γκαίριγκ|Hermann Göring|Hermann Göring was a German politician and military officer of the Nazi regime. He commanded the Luftwaffe and was one of Hitler's close associates. He was sentenced to death at the Nuremberg trial but committed suicide in 1946.

bio|01-12|1949|Χαρούκι Μουρακάμι|Haruki Murakami|Haruki Murakami is a Japanese writer. He has written novels such as "Norwegian Wood" and "Kafka on the Shore". His books have been translated into many languages and he is one of the best-known contemporary writers of Japan.
